newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Palm Oil/Laurics-Asia prices seen mixed.
newsitem.headline: Palm Oil/Laurics-Asia prices seen mixed.

text.p: Asian palm and laurics oil prices are likely to trade uncertainly this week, with a bearish USDA crop production report on Friday and lack of supportive factors seen pulling down palm prices in Malaysia and Singapore.

Regional traders said the palm markets were also waiting for private crop forecaster Ivan Wong's report on Monday and key Palm Oil Registration and Licensing Authority (PORLA) September crop data on Tuesday.
"We are likely to see palm oil prices falling at the opening Monday due to sharply lower soyoil on the bearish USDA report," a trader in Malaysia said.
A trader from Singapore said the bearish report could send prices of Malaysia's third month December futures sliding below 1,150 ringgit. On Friday, the contract closed at 1,157 ringgit.
Malaysian traders said palm prices could ease further if PORLA announces a set of bearish September crop data.
Wong, who may release September data on Monday, earlier projected output in September would rise by four percent to 843,000 tonnes over August and end-September stocks would stand at 905,000 tonnes.
With Indian demand slowing as the soybean harvest begins there, and Chinese buying just holding steady, prices would have a bearish tone, Singapore traders said.
Major buyers have been absent from the palm markets where players feel current prices are unattractive.
In Indonesia, palm olein prices are showing some downside potential due to weak sentiment and mounting selling pressure.
Indonesian traders said sentiment turned weak following President Suharto's recent call for market operations by state logistics agency BULOG to control prices of essential commodities.
BULOG intervenes in the palm oil market, for instance, by importing olein and offering it for sale at below market levels, forcing the private sector to lower its prices.

Traders in Indonesia said local prices were at a premium to European values and sellers preferred to sell locally. "There is still a slight premium in the local market, and this is why some players have been offering very competitive prices," an Indonesian trader said.
The trader also said fresh shipments of palm olein were expected to arrive this week, keeping supply adequate.

Traders expect coconut oil prices to trade at $700 to $705 per tonne FOB. In the previous week, Philippines traders projected a steady rise in prices on delayed copra harvest as a result of persistent rains in certain copra-rich areas in Mindanao in the southern Philippines.
Traders said the weather had started to improve last week.
